items.t: Nestlé Pakistan’s Sustainability Journey Recognized at SDC and SIE
sum: Practical action across operations, farms and communities, bringing together sustainability commitments to life were in focus at the 29th Sustainable Development Conference (SDC) and Sustainability Investment Expo (SIE) in Islamabad, where Nestlé Pakistan showcased its journey across climate action, regenerative agriculture and circularity.

The company’s efforts were recognized with two accolades at the conference: the Sustainability Award in the Circular Economy & Resource Efficiency category and the Best Pavilion Presentation Award. The recognition came alongside Nestlé Pakistan’s participation in conversations around the future of sustainable food systems, including a high-level plenary on “Transforming Pakistan’s Agriculture and Food Systems in an Age of Disruption: AI for Regenerative and Climate-Smart Agriculture.”

The conference and expo also provided an opportunity to engage policymakers and other stakeholders around some of the practical interventions already underway. Rana Tanveer Hussain, Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research, and Shezra Mansab, Minister of State for Climate Change, were among the senior government representatives who visited Nestlé Pakistan’s exhibition, which brought together initiatives spanning regenerative agriculture, climate action, water stewardship and circularity.

Nestlé Pakistan also co-hosted a high-level plenary titled “Transforming Pakistan’s Agriculture and Food Systems in an Age of Disruption: AI for Regenerative and Climate-Smart Agriculture” at the conference.

Opening the discussion on Nestlé Pakistan’s efforts and initiatives, Faisal Nadeem, Head of Technical, Nestlé Pakistan, shared, “With cultivable land under increasing pressure and soil health declining, the need to transition towards regenerative agriculture has never been greater. The encouraging part is that soil health can be restored. At Nestlé, we are working with farmers and partners to scale regenerative practices that improve soil health, improve water efficiency, and strengthen resilience to climate pressures.”

SMI slips 0.29% to 15,106.12 points on Friday close
sum: Индекс швейцарского рынка завершил пятницу, 13 ноября 2026 года, на отметке 15 106,12 пункта, что на 43,31 пункта, или 0,29 процента, ниже уровня закрытия четверга в 15 149,43 пункта. Цифры и диапазон сессии сообщил finanzen.ch.

Индекс открылся на отметке 15 107,95 пункта, что уже на 0,274 процента ниже предыдущего закрытия. Он поднялся до максимума в 15 130,68 пункта и минимума в 15 037,34 пункта, прежде чем завершиться на отрицательной территории. Снижение последовало за ростом на 0,63% в четверг, когда SMI достиг рекордного внутридневного максимума в 15 200,17 пункта и закрылся на отметке 15 149,43.

Акции Richemont упали на 3,80 процента, что сделало владельца Cartier одним из самых слабых участников SMI. Yahoo Finance сообщила, что чистая прибыль в первом полугодии выросла до 2,5 млрд евро с 1,8 млрд евро годом ранее, но рост продаж ювелирных изделий на 14 процентов оказался ниже 16 процентов, ожидаемых в опросе РБК. Ближний Восток, особенно Объединенные Арабские Эмираты, был слабым местом в ювелирном бизнесе.

Выдвинулись несколько имен, связанных с обороной и здравоохранением. Акции Alcon прибавили 1,79 процента, Nestlé - 1,33 процента, Swiss Life - 0,93 процента, Zurich Insurance - 0,71 процента, а Swiss Re - 0,66 процента. По данным finanzen.ch, акции Sandoz упали на 2,65 процента, Galderma - на 1,54 процента, Sika - на 1,01 процента, а Holcim - на 0,96 процента.

Инвесторы также столкнулись со сложной международной ситуацией. LGT указала на неопределенность вокруг смены руководства Nvidia, более высоких цен на нефть и ожиданий дополнительного повышения процентных ставок в США. Эти темы оставались актуальными для настроений к риску, поскольку европейские рынки приближались к выходным.

Nestlé confirms Quality Street chocolate box change for Christmas 2026
sum: The company made the decision after a two-year trial in Tesco stores

Nestlé has confirmed a change for its Christmas Quality Street tubs. The company has decided to scrap its cardboard tubs this festive season after trialling the eco-conscious packaging over two years.

The two-year trial, which saw cardboard tubs at select Tesco supermarkets, comes to an end this Christmas. It was a controversial packaging change that followed Quality Street's switch to paper wrappers for its sweets.

The cardboard container, presented in the iconic Quality Street purple, was marketed as having "a luxurious design and feel, and embellished with gold foil" - while being able to be disposed of with household recycling.

First Holdco, Dangote Cement, Aradel drive 60% NGX surge after FTSE reclassification
sum: The Nigerian Exchange (NGX) has recorded a strong rally this year, led by heavyweight stocks including First Holdco, Dangote Cement, Aradel Holdings, Zenith Bank and Guaranty Trust Holding Company (GTCO), as Nigeria’s return to the FTSE Russell Frontier Market classification draws renewed attention to its largest listed companies.

The market’s nearly 60 percent year-to-date (YtD) gain reflects a combination of improved investor sentiment, expectations surrounding the FTSE reclassification and strong price appreciation among large-cap stocks. Other major performers include MTN Nigeria Communications, Stanbic IBTC Holdings, Nestlé Nigeria, Nigerian Breweries and Presco.

FTSE Russell confirmed Nigeria’s return to Frontier Market status in late August 2026, with the reclassification taking effect on September 21 following its semi-annual review. The development brought Nigerian equities back into the radar of international investors tracking frontier-market benchmarks.

Ten Nigerian companies were included in the FTSE Frontier Index Series: Guaranty Trust Holding Company, Zenith Bank, MTN Nigeria Communications, Dangote Cement and Stanbic IBTC Holdings. Others are First Holdco, Nestlé Nigeria, Nigerian Breweries, Presco and Aradel Holdings.

Ahead of the reclassification, investors positioned themselves in anticipation of increased foreign portfolio interest, helping drive a broad market rally between January and early September. The NGX All-Share Index gained between 58 and 60 percent year-to-date in local currency terms, while returns exceeded 70 percent in dollar terms.
On September 21, the day the reclassification took effect, the NGX All-Share Index stood at 250,156.80 points, while total market capitalisation crossed N162 trillion.
The rally subsequently pushed the market’s valuation beyond N165 trillion, reinforcing the growing importance of Nigerian equities in frontier-market investment portfolios.

Everton Women agree sweet deal with Nestlé
sum: November 8 – Everton Women have signed Nestlé Confectionery as official chocolate and grab-bag sweet partner, in only the second dedicated commercial deal for the women’s team.

Nestlé also becomes an official supplier of both club venues: Goodison Park, where the women play most of their games, and Hill Dickinson Stadium, the men’s home and the club’s designated main stadium. Under WSL rules, the women must play at least one match a season there.
KitKat, Smarties, Aero, Lion, Yorkie, Milkybar and Quality Street will be sold at both grounds. At Goodison, Nestlé gets pitch side LED advertising, big-screen exposure and matchday activations.

“Working collaboratively with Everton Football Club, we’ll bring the No.1 confectionery single within the leisure channel, KitKat 4 Finger, along with other iconic Nestlé Confectionery brands for everyone to enjoy,” said Gail Stove, out-of-home confectionery lead for Nestlé UK & Ireland.

Andrew Middleton, Everton’s president of business operations, said: “Like Everton, Nestlé’s brands have been part of family life for generations, making this a natural fit for our supporters and matchday experience. This partnership is another important step in Everton Women’s continued growth.”

The women’s team’s only other standalone partner is catering company GGM Gastro, signed last year. Most of the club’s other sponsorships cover the men’s team. Building a separate commercial base for the women matters as WSL clubs try to become financially self-sustaining rather than relying on the men’s side.

The deal arrives during a period of uncertainty at the top. The Friedkin Group, which bought a majority stake from Farhad Moshiri in December 2024, has reportedly hired Moelis & Company to explore selling part or all of its holding, less than two years after taking over.

Two companies interested in talking to Nestlé
sum: Two of the region’s leading food manufacturers have expressed interest in exploring the future of Nestlé Trinidad and Tobago’s dairy and juices business if the company opens discussions with potential buyers.

Nestlé announced on July 2 that it had begun a strategic review of its T&T operations as part of a wider global restructuring. The company said it is exploring several options for the dairy and juices business, including a possible sale. More than 200 workers are employed at its Valsayn facility along the Churchill-Roosevelt Highway.

Business Guardian reached out to several businesses following Nestlé’s announcement. While most said it was too early in the process to indicate whether they would be interested in acquiring the business, Richard Pandohie, the CEO of Seprod—the Jamaican conglomerate which is the parent company of T&T’s AS Bryden & Sons Holdings— and Hadco Limited group co-CEO John Hadad both said they would remain open to discussions if the opportunity arises.
Pandohie said Seprod is familiar with Nestlé’s operations through previous business dealings.
“Nestlé is an excellent organisation and operation that we know well. We have worked with them on various projects,” he said.
“In fact, Seprod Jamaica bought from Nestlé internationally, globally a few years ago. So, it’s an amazing organisation.”
He indicated there have been no discussions between the companies.

Nestlé Backs Full-Year Targets as Ski Sponsorship and U.S. Plant Shift Reshape the Story
sum: Nestlé has reaffirmed its 2026 guidance, keeping its organic growth target of 3% to 4% intact alongside a free cash flow forecast above CHF 9 billion. The confirmation, first issued with third-quarter results roughly two weeks ago, also points to an improvement in the underlying operating margin compared with 2025.

Those quarterly figures, released for Q3 2026, showed sales of CHF 22.756 billion. Organic growth came in at 4.0%, of which 2.8% represented real internal growth. Reuters reported at the time that the stock initially gained ground following the release.

The shares have since lost some altitude. Nestlé fell 1.4% in yesterday's trading, with no specific company catalyst identified in Friday's market coverage. A separate report put today's decline at 1.2%, attributing the pressure to a weaker Swiss market, where soft U.S. leads had followed a sell-off in AI-related stocks after the congressional election. No link to any analyst action has been established for either move.

Alongside its commercial performance, Nestlé has moved to raise the profile of several key brands through winter sport. The company and Swiss-Ski announced a three-year partnership on 29 October, under which Nestlé becomes an official Silver Partner. No contract value was disclosed.

The agreement puts Cailler, Thomy and Nescafé on show across a range of snow sports and at events, while also funding young skiing talent. Media reports said the partners signed the deal at Nestlé Switzerland's headquarters, and that the collaboration begins with the current season. That opening season coincides with the World Ski Championships in Crans-Montana, scheduled for 1 to 14 February 2027.

On the operational side, Nestlé USA told employees on 19 October that it will close its Solon, Ohio, production site by the end of 2027, according to media reports. Output of Nestlé Professional Solutions pouches is to be shifted in stages to Gaffney, South Carolina.
Investors will get their next full update on 18 February 2027, the expected date for the fourth-quarter 2026 results.

Climate pressures mount on Vietnam's coffee sector
sum: The information was shared by Binu Jacob, CEO of Nestlé Vietnam at the 'Shaping the Future' discussion session during the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit on November 3.

Jacob said, “There is no single solution or technology to address these challenges and enhance the competitiveness of Vietnamese coffee beans. It is vital to combine suitable coffee varieties, soil conditions, water management, and experience sharing among farming households to develop production efficiency.”

Nestlé has prioritised the development of coffee varieties suited to local soil conditions in the Central Highlands. According to Jacob, Nestlé has partnered with the Western Highlands Agriculture and Forestry Science Institute (WASI) to research the varieties.

One of Nestlé's priorities in the Central Highlands is developing coffee varieties suited to local soil conditions. According to Jacob, the company has partnered with WASI to research disease-resistant coffee varieties that require less water and pesticides.

At the same time, the development of suitable coffee varieties must be accompanied by the capacity for propagation, enabling large-scale implementation. Through tissue culture techniques, a single coffee leaf can be used to propagate approximately 2,000 seedlings. Over the past 15 years, the programme has produced 100 million disease-resistant coffee varieties and distributed them to farmers in the Central Highlands at subsidised prices.

Jacob said, “The solution is vital to address several ageing coffee plantations. Coffee yields typically begin to decline after around seven to 10 years, creating a need for replanting to maintain production efficiency.”

“To ensure the coffee supply in long term, attention should be paid to restore health and manage water resources through regenerative farming practices,” he said. “Once properly implemented, reducing water and pesticide can improve economic returns without lowering yields.”

Vietnamese agricultural products: To maintain exports, investment must start from the source.
sum: Southeast Asia plays a crucial role in the global agricultural supply chain, but also faces increasing pressure from climate change, consumer demand, and fluctuations in international trade. For countries with strong agricultural export capabilities like Vietnam, the question is not only how to maintain production levels, but also how to ensure a stable domestic supply while continuing to meet the demands of the global market.

Speaking at the "Shaping the Future" discussion session within the framework of the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit on November 3rd, Mr. Binu Jacob, General Director of Nestlé Vietnam , stated that the key lies in enhancing the agricultural value chain through long-term investment in farmers, improving farming methods, and developing value-added products.
These are also the factors that determine the ability to maintain the supply of agricultural products in the context of production facing many pressures.

When asked about technologies or methods that could revolutionize agricultural production in the Central Highlands – an area with a long dry season and unique soil conditions – Mr. Binu Jacob stated that no single solution would be sufficient to address all the challenges.

According to him, production efficiency depends on a combination of many factors, from suitable crop varieties, soil conditions, and water utilization to farmers learning from and sharing experiences with each other.

In this context, Mr. Binu Jacob identified plant science as one of the most important factors. He also cited the example of Nestlé's collaboration with the Western Highlands Agro-Forestry Science and Technology Institute (WASI) to develop a coffee variety suitable for the region's soil. This variety is disease-resistant, requires less water, and reduces the need for pesticides. Through tissue culture techniques, approximately 2,000 plants can be propagated from a single coffee leaf.
He said that over the past 15 years, the program has produced 100 million disease-resistant coffee seedlings and distributed them to farmers in the Central Highlands at subsidized prices.

India’s consumers are back, its stocks aren’t
sum: India’s economy and its stock market are not seeing eye to eye.

As the nation begins its busiest part of the year marked by a string of Hindu festivals and monsoon harvests, consumer demand is skyrocketing. Companies selling everything from shampoos to jewelry to baby formula to watches are reporting robust demand — and even managing to raise prices. Yet the stocks of bellwethers like Hindustan Unilever Ltd. and Maruti Suzuki India Ltd. have sunk to multiyear lows.

Indian stocks have underperformed global markets for more than two years, losing nearly half their value, as foreign capital fled. Disappointing earnings, scant exposure to the artificial-intelligence boom, and external shocks such as US tariffs and oil-price spikes from the Iran war have all weighed on returns. As global money managers ran out of reasons to invest, some bulls nursed one hope — that once consumer demand accelerated, corporate earnings would improve, offsetting the drag and reviving returns.

Now, even that flicker is being doused. The latest quarterly results show that a consumption boom is unlikely to end stocks’ underperformance. We may well be heading into a paradoxical period — rapid economic growth co-existing with an equity market in the doldrums.

Consumer demand among the country’s 1.5 billion people is coming back with a roar. The e-commerce market is heading for its fastest growth in five years and will hit a record $90 billion in 2026, according to Redseer Strategy Consultants. The trend growth in consumer demand has moved up a couple of notches, according to official data.
From consumer-goods company Dabur India Ltd. to Nestlé India Ltd. to jeweler Titan Co., businesses are reporting double-digit sales growth. Most are hiking prices because of robust demand.

But that’s not enough for investors. They are now valuing resilience more than headline growth. The question is no longer simply how fast companies can expand, but how much of that growth they can convert into profits when higher input costs, taxes and other pressures are eating into margins. Shareholders have little appetite for consumer companies pursuing growth by surrendering profit margins.

This is why Kit Kat is a symbol of good luck in Japan
sum: In Japan, Kit Kat is so much more than a chocolate sweet – it's a little good-luck charm! The name sounds almost exactly like a Japanese phrase for "you'll surely win," and the chocolate has become everything from an exam good-luck charm to a postcard and a train ticket.

If you've ever travelled to Japan, you've surely noticed it: Kit Kat is everywhere, in flavours you've never seen back home and in packaging that looks like little presents. Behind the popularity lies a delightful story about language, happiness and thoughtfulness – and about how a piece of chocolate can become a symbol of hope.

It all starts with a happy coincidence. The expression "kitto katsu" means roughly "you will surely win" in the dialect of Kyushu in southern Japan – and it sounds almost exactly like Kit Kat. According to Nestlé Japan, students began giving each other the chocolate as a good luck charm ahead of the tough entrance exams in the late 1990s. Kit Kat had by then existed in Japan since 1973, and the company has run campaigns around the exams since 2003.

Today the tradition is deeply rooted. In a survey by Nestlé, as reported by Japan Post, one in three students stated that they buy Kit Kat before the exam and one in five that they bring the chocolate into the exam hall. And as recently as February 2026, 1,250 drones lit up the sky over a shrine in Hofu with a blossoming cherry tree – a good-luck greeting to everyone about to sit an exam.

In 2009, Nestlé and Japan Post took the idea a step further with Kit Kat Mail. The packaging of four Kit Kats, adorned with cherry blossoms, had space for an address and a personal message and could be sent directly from the post office – like a postcard filled with happiness. According to Japan Post, the set with a stamp was sold for 450 yen and only at post offices, and the campaign won the Grand Prix in the media category at the Cannes Lions advertising festival that same year, as the first Japanese company in that category.
The idea became a success and came back in new versions for several years – including bookmarks with poems, a small daruma doll and a fold-out box with a cherry tree.
The most moving part of the story takes place along the coast in north-eastern Japan.

items.t: Nestlé bets on “fewer, bigger” innovations to drive scalable food growth
sum: - Nestlé is prioritizing fewer, scalable innovation platforms that combine global reach with locally tailored products.
- Convenience and changing consumption occasions drive developments across desserts, snacking, iced coffee, and GLP-1 nutrition.
- Emerging-market growth and portfolio consolidation support Nestlé’s focus on core brands spanning indulgence, convenience, and health.

Nestlé is rolling out a new generation of dessert solutions in Brazil and China. The move illustrates how the food giant is concentrating its innovation resources on scalable platforms that can be adapted to local tastes and emerging consumption occasions.

The launches span Moça Pudding and Brigadeirão in Brazil and Nestlé Tiramisù and Cheesecake in China. Consumers can prepare the desserts in three steps, with less than 15 minutes of active preparation time.

Nestlé positions the range as part of its modern cooking growth platform, which seeks to translate the company’s culinary expertise into complete, convenient solutions rather than individual ingredients. According to consumer research cited by Nestlé, 84% of consumers say they would bake more often if it were easier.
“Combining global scale with local relevance is how we continue to grow and innovate,” says Stephanie Arnesen, category lead for dairy culinary solutions at Nestlé’s Food Strategic Business Unit.

Nestlé: Coffee sustainability key to avoiding cocoa-like crisis
sum: In 2025, the cocoa industry was hit with one of the worst crises in several decades where prices hit record highs of over US$10,950 /MT, caused by a culmination of factors such as severe crop failure, climate change and plant disease.

Even though prices corrected back to below US$4,000/MT early this year, the industry is already digging its heels in to prepare for another production deficit in the upcoming season, largely due to incoming El Niño weather.

Together, this is causing one of the most severe instabilities the global cocoa industry has faced in a long time, and because weather and climate have been the most widely-attributed reasons for this, it also means that various other crops are also susceptible to similar challenges — with coffee having been widely named as one as it grows in a similar tropical environment as cocoa, with the same rainfall and temperature reliance.

As such, coffee companies worldwide are also working to improve resilience and reduce risk to production yields, in hopes of avoiding the same fate as cocoa has. One of these is Nestle, owner of major global coffee brands like Nescafe and Nespresso.

“Nestle’s main strategy to ensure coffee sustainability [and supply stability] is the Nescafe Plan 2030, which is all about making coffee farming future-proof,” Nestle Chief Communications and Sustainability Officer Antonia Wanner said.

“Even though we are seeing more and more extreme weather patterns such as longer droughts and stark rains which makes things very stressful for the plants and of course for the farmers, we have seen that through agricultural methods like regenerative agriculture, the farms are actually more resilient.”

The plan is an undoubtedly ambitious one, tying in with wider business goals to make the business fully net zero by 2050 and have regenerative agricultural practices applied for 50% of its sourced ingredients. And amid all of these, coffee is taking an undeniable front seat.

sum: European shares fell on Thursday as chip stocks slid and Nestlé tumbled, while investors concluded that a European Central Bank (ECB) rate hike remains in play in September, even as it kept rates at its latest governing council meeting after increasing official borrowing costs last month.

Geopolitical concerns added to the pressure. After months of investor focus on the Strait of Hormuz, attention has shifted to the Red Sea where Iranian-aligned Houthis, who control areas near the Bab el-Mandeb strait, have opened a new front in the Middle East crisis.
Brent crude futures rose past $100 (€87.90) a barrel, their highest since late May. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index fell 1.2 per cent.

The Iseq All-Share index slid 2.4 per cent to 13,317.39. Ryanair plunged 5.1 per cent to €23.32, as rising oil prices weighed on market sentiment towards the carrier, days after it reported weaker-than-expected results. Fellow travel-related firm Irish Continental Group (ICG) fell 1.6 per cent to €6.30.

Banks were also out of favour, with AIB off 1.9 per cent at €10.64, while Bank of Ireland slipped 0.6 per cent to €18.21. PTSB dipped 0.3 per cent to €3.02, but remained ahead of the €2.97 price that Austrian bank Bawag has agreed to buy the lender for, subject to approval at a PTSB extraordinary general meeting next week.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index fell 0.7 per cent to 10,639.2 points, reversing most of the previous session’s 1 per cent rise. Precious metal miners dropped 5.1 per cent as gold prices fell around 2 per cent on a stronger dollar and rising inflation concerns due to the oil-price spike.
Travel and leisure shares retreated 1.9 per cent with shares of airlines including Wizz leading declines as higher oil prices weighed.

sum: Nestlé India reported an impressive financial performance for the first quarter of FY27, with consolidated net profit rising 48.26% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹958.68 crore, compared with ₹646.59 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. The strong earnings were driven by robust volume growth, higher domestic sales, premiumisation, and continued expansion across urban and rural markets.

The FMCG major also reported a 25.16% increase in consolidated revenue from operations to ₹6,378.18 crore, reflecting strong consumer demand across its product portfolio. Following the announcement, Nestlé India shares were trading at ₹1,479.70, up 1.79%, after touching an intraday high of ₹1,510.
Nestlé India delivered healthy growth across key financial metrics during the April–June quarter.
The strong performance was largely supported by higher sales volumes, continued consumer demand, and disciplined execution across distribution channels.
Nestlé India shares reacted positively to the quarterly earnings announcement.
The positive movement reflects investor confidence in the company’s strong earnings, consistent volume growth, and long-term growth strategy.

Commenting on the quarterly performance, Chairman and Managing Director Manish Tiwary said the company delivered strong sales growth driven primarily by higher volumes and sustained consumer trust in Nestlé’s brands.

Nestlé Opens First Railway NESCAFÉ Kiosk
sum: Nestlé Professional, the out-of-home business division of Nestlé India, has expanded its presence in the travel retail segment with the launch of a NESCAFÉ kiosk at Thrissur Railway Station in Kerala. The outlet is the company's first kiosk under its partnership with Indian Railways and is designed to serve passengers with a range of food and beverage offerings during their journeys. Located at one of Kerala's busiest railway stations, the kiosk offers hot and cold coffee beverages along with selected food products.

Saurabh Makhija, Head, Nestlé Professional said, "Indian Railways touches the lives of millions of Indians every day and has earned a place of immense trust in the hearts of consumers across the country. Being associated with such an iconic institution is a matter of great pride for us. With the launch of our NESCAFÉ outlet at Thrissur Railway Station, we are delighted to bring travellers a comforting and familiar experience through quality coffee and trusted food and beverage offerings during their journeys."

Jinraj Adyanthaya, Sales Head, Nestlé Professional added, “Railways is a very important channel for Nestlé Professional, given its scale and ability to connect with millions of consumers on the move every day. This new initiative with Indian Railways will enable us to further expand our presence across the network while bringing a wider range of Nestle’s food and beverage offerings to consumers on the move. We intend to participate in as many tenders as possible across railway divisions throughout India under this initiative, helping us strengthen our footprint in the travel segment and make our trusted brands more accessible to consumers. All outlets will be operated through Nestlé-authorized operators to ensure consistent quality, service, and consumer experience."

The launch forms part of Nestlé Professional's strategy to strengthen its footprint across high-traffic travel locations and create more out-of-home consumption opportunities for its brands. The company also noted that the new kiosk builds on its Retail ONE network, which has crossed 1,000 kiosks across India. These outlets are located across educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and travel destinations.

Nestlé opens automated distribution center in California
sum: Nestlé USA opened a $330 million, 700,000-square-foot distribution center in Arvin, California, it announced in June.

The Swiss food and beverage company called the new facility its largest and most technologically advanced distribution center to date. Its new facility will use automation to improve efficiency and eventually get all of its energy from renewable sources, including wind and solar, it said.
Nestlé operates 335 factories in 75 countries. The Americas, including the United States, are its largest market and accounted for 48% of sales in 2025.

“Our investment in the new Arvin Distribution Center reflects how we’re building Nestlé for the future, modernizing our supply chain and delivering for our customers and consumers with greater speed and precision,” said Marty Thompson, chief executive officer, in a written statement.
Nestlé is No. 10 in the Europe Database. The market research tool tracks that region’s largest 500 online retailers based on their annual ecommerce sales.

The facility’s technology centerpiece is its Automated Storage and Retrieval System. Nestlé said it’s the largest within its global network. It designed the technology to handle the movement of shelf-stable goods with improved accuracy through laser-guided vehicles and robotics.

The company also said it designed the site for flexible operations to handle demand swings across its portfolio and support future growth. Products from brands including Nestlé Toll House, Coffee mate and Gerber will move through the facility.

sum: Morning Trade: Nestlé India Shares up 2.35% Despite Broader Market Selloff
Mumbai, April 22: Nestlé India is another stock that defied the carnage in broader markets to open with a green bias on Wednesday morning following Tuesday’s results-driven rally.

As of 9:40 am on Wednesday, the stock is trading in the ₹1,412–₹1,413 range after opening at ₹1,391 in the pre-market session, marking a gain of around 2.35% on Tuesday’s closing price of ₹1,379.90. The stock has clearly shrugged off intraday weakness after the news-driven spike on Tuesday, attracting buyers at lower levels throughout the session and continuing to climb despite minor corrections — investors seem to have marked Tuesday’s closing price as a “buying opportunity.” Nestle’s gains come even as the Sensex dropped by around 550 points in Wednesday’s morning session. Viewed in this light, Nestle has clearly been one of the best performers so far today.

As can be seen in the chart below, Nestlé India gapped up at the open on Wednesday. Between 9 and 9:15 am, the stock moved up steadily from around ₹1,383 to open at ₹1,391. At 9:15 am when exchanges opened for the day, the stock surged to an intraday high of around ₹1,419–₹1,420, before correcting violently to about ₹1,401 at around 9:30 am. While the sell-off was fairly intense, this sort of quick down-move in a stock that is showing strength is usually healthy since it helps flush out short-term traders looking to bank their profits.

From the ₹1,401 level, Nestle climbed through ₹1,407–₹1,413 where it was trading around 9:40 am and remained steady in that range through 10:15 am, even touching a secondary intraday high of around ₹1,422 at around 10 am. This sort of activity indicates that demand continues to outstrip supply near current levels.

The chart below showcases Nestle’s stellar price action over the last five trading sessions. Nestle India traded sideways around ₹1,256 on April 15 and again at ₹1,257 on April 16, before jumping to around ₹1,285 on April 17 on positive pre-results sentiment. It maintained those levels through April 20, before breaking out sharply on Tuesday to close at around ₹1,393, marking a 5-day return of nearly 11%.

sum: Nestle shares rose 3% Thursday after the maker of Nescafé and KitKat reported organic sales growth for the fourth quarter that beat analyst forecasts.

The closely watched organic sales growth rate came in at 4%, beating a FactSet consensus of 3.55%. For 2026, Nestle said it is targeting organic sales growth of 3% to 4%, along with an improvement in its underlying trading operating profit margin, which stood at 16.1% in 2025.
The Vevey, Switzerland-based company also announced it was planning to sell its remaining ice cream business to Haagen-Dazs owner Froneri, a joint venture by PAI and Nestle.

In addition, Nestle said it started the formal process to shed its water business earlier in the first quarter, and expects the business, which holds brands such as Henniez and Perrier to be deconsolidated by 2027.
Shares were last trading up 2.6% and the stock is up around 2% so far this year.

The company, under its new leadership duo of CEO Philipp Navratil and Chairman Pablo Isla, a former Inditex executive, have been focusing on streamlining the sprawling consumer giant, after years of operational and share-price underperformance.

"We are accelerating our strategy. We are focusing our portfolio on four businesses, led by our strongest brands, with prioritized resources and a simplified organization," Navratil said in a statement.

sum: Navratil is in the midst of slashing 16,000 jobs, or about 6% of the global workforce, reorganising the business around four core divisions, and managing the baby formula recall.

(Feb 19): Nestlé SA's new chief executive officer shrugged off the biggest infant formula recall in the Swiss foodmaker's history with an upbeat outlook for the year and the planned sale of its remaining ice cream brands.

CEO Philipp Navratil said the turnaround at the company — whose performance has lagged for years — is on track as he forecast sales and profit growth and revealed plans to reorganise the 160-year-old group. Nestlé shares rose the most in four months.
"Our actions are starting to pay off and the growth trends are improving," Navratil told analysts on a call. "We have a clear strategy with priorities."

The maker of Nespresso coffee and Purina cat chow on Thursday forecast organic revenue growth of 3% to 4% in 2026. That compares with the 3.2% estimate of analysts in a Bloomberg survey. Real internal growth — a closely watched measure of volumes — will accelerate in 2026, the company said.

Navratil has endured a torrid start since taking over the top job in September following the ouster of his predecessor over an undisclosed office romance. He is in the midst of slashing 16,000 jobs, or about 6% of the global workforce, reorganising the business around four core divisions, and managing the baby formula recall.
Nestlé said it's ahead on its cost-cutting plan and has already achieved around 20% of the targeted savings.
